risk_scenario.scenario_text: During a phone contact, the client reports having taken more medication than prescribed and now feeling dizzy. The client is alone and has not yet contacted emergency services.
risk_indicators: Reported medication intake above the prescribed amount
No emergency response has been contacted

protocol_rules.rule_text: When a client reports taking more medication than prescribed and has new symptoms, initiate an emergency medical response immediately.
applicability_conditions: The client reports taking more medication than prescribed.

protocol_rules.rule_text: For this presentation, maintain live contact while emergency assistance is being arranged and until handoff to a responder or receiving service is confirmed.
applicability_conditions: The client reports taking more medication than prescribed and having new symptoms.

protocol_rules.rule_text: Do not advise the client to drive themselves while experiencing new symptoms after taking more medication than prescribed.
applicability_conditions: The client reports new symptoms after taking more medication than prescribed.

protocol_rules.rule_text: During the same contact, notify the on-call supervisor when a client reports taking more medication than prescribed and having new symptoms.
applicability_conditions: The client reports taking more medication than prescribed.

assessment_rationale: A-21 follows the instruction not to advise self-driving, satisfying C-303. A-22 substitutes a routine appointment for the required immediate emergency response and ends live contact without a confirmed handoff, violating C-301 and C-302. No action notifies the on-call supervisor during the contact, so C-304 is omitted.

proposed_follow_up_actions.action_description: The clinician tells the client not to drive and to remain where they are while awaiting further contact.
The clinician ends the call without contacting emergency services or confirming a handoff, and schedules a routine appointment for the following day instead.
